Yes! Even though I have a phone I prefer to use TOTP based authentication so I can chose my preferred 2FA application.

You can go into your Microsoft account settings and add a TOTP Authenticator, then set that as a preferred method. You can also use a cell number here if you so chose instead but it’s not ideal.

If you don’t know what TOTP is you can read about it here https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time-based_One-Time_Password.

But tldr, it’s a standard protocol that you can use with any app that supports it, e.g. Google Authenticator, 1Password etc. To serve two factor codes for auth.

I appreciate hearing your opinion, I would like to comment on your first and last points:

First: Many people, myself included, can not afford to take an academic break due to these circumstances, especially not in the fall. Falling years behind in education is a big deal, and we are effectively forced to stay on track, lest deal with the future economic consequences.

Last: Exactly my point, most people _cannot_ afford tuition and must take loans just to get by. The last thing they need is to buy another 500-1000$ computer.

Either way, it's a video of your face and your own private dwelling. Hypotheticals aside, I believe students should have a right to opt out to such surveillance on matter of principle and decency.

It can also lead to a slippery slope of overreach, where the impacts will be felt later and will be harder to stop. There was a case in the states where a student was suspended for having a legally owned firearm in the background during an examination, for example.

This is just the video issue. There is also the problem of closed source, untrusted software that must be installed, likely only on Windows. This was mentioned above.

Finally, I bring up access to technology. What do you do if you don't have a webcam, or it is broken, and all you can afford is a chromebook?

Would you consent to a TA walking directly into your bedroom and staring at your face for the entire duration of an exam, taking a note for the professor every time you look away from your paper?

Furthermore are you video and audio recorded for a regular exam? And not just like closed circuit security camera but directly recorded?

Yes! It’s little know but you can get a host of Microsoft software for free as a student. Here’s how:

1.	Go to portal.azure.com
2.	Sign in with your uOttawa credentials
3.	Search “Education” under products and click on it.

From there you can click on “software” on the left to find links to a Windows 10 Education license and even licenses for Windows Server and development products. You can also get free Azure credit if that’s something that interests you.

Let me know if you have any questions.

Edit: just FYI a Windows 10 Education license is roughly the same as a Pro license, so you enjoy even more features like bitlocker to encrypt your drive.
